newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees higher steel production in 1997.
newsitem.headline: EU sees higher steel production in 1997.

text.p: Steel production in the European Union may rise by some 6.5 percent to 157 million tonnes in 1997, the European Commission said on Friday.
It also said internal EU steel prices should rise further in coming months.

"The business upswing for the main steel consuming industries, which need to build up stocks of finished products to meet both increased domestic demand and export commitments, points to faster growth in Community steel production over the coming months," it said in a steel report in its Official Journal.
It said 1997 production could therefore exceed "the outstanding level" achieved in 1995, when output amounted to 155.7 million tonnes.

"The gradual restoration of a more satisfactory steel production rate will no doubt help to improve the utilisation rate of capacity and improve operating profits, which is highly desirable if Community producers are to be more efficient."
The Commission said the trend towards stabilisation of steel prices in the EU observed in the last months of 1996 was confirmed from the beginning of this year.
However, it said the recovery in prices had only partly offset the cumulative losses of the preceding period.

"Moreover, Community steel prices are still much lower than those on the world market...Internal prices should therefore rise further in the coming months with the better prospects of growth for the second half of 1997 in the EU and the probable maintenance of the current rate of the dollar which favours Community exports."
